PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Islam teaches Muslims to work hard and to help people who are truly in need. Begging, when a person is able to work, is discouraged because it harms dignity and the community. In this sub-strand you will name the people who deserve help, describe the evils of begging, and see how honest work helps to remove poverty.

## Strand 5.0: Akhlaq (Moral Teachings)
Sub-strand 5.2.1: Prohibitions in Islam: Evils of Begging
Suggested lessons: 2

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) identify categories of people who deserve assistance in society
b) describe the evils of begging as a means of fostering hard work
c) appreciate work as a means of eradicating poverty

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why do people beg?
2. Why is begging discouraged?

## Core competencies
• Communication and collaboration: the skill of listening and speaking as learners discuss evils of begging according to the teachings of Islam and present in class.
• Critical thinking and problem solving: the skill of researching as learners discuss ways of earning income/ generating income and present in class

## Values
• Responsibility enhanced as learners take turns to discuss evils of begging according to the teachings of Islam and present in class.
• Integrity is enhanced as learners discuss ways of earning income/ generating income and present in class

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Life skills: Self-awareness to avoid begging without justification

## Links to other learning areas
• Social Studies as learners are encouraged to work and contribute to nation building.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 5.0 Akhlaq (Moral Teachings), Sub-strand 5.2.1 Prohibitions in Islam: Evils of Begging
• Sahih Muslim: begging is not permissible except for three cases (debt, calamity, and confirmed poverty)
• Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim: the upper hand is better than the lower hand; Sahih al-Bukhari: earning by one's own hands, and selling firewood rather than begging

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Who deserves help, and why begging is an evil

LESSON 1: WHO DESERVES HELP, AND WHY BEGGING IS AN EVIL
=======================================================

## What you will learn
• Name the categories of people who deserve assistance.
• Explain why people beg.
• Describe the evils of begging according to Islamic teachings.

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify categories of people who deserve assistance in society; b) describe the evils of begging as a means of fostering hard work

## Introduction
At the market you may see someone sitting with a hand stretched out, asking passers-by for money. Islam does not ignore people who are suffering, but it also warns against begging when a person can earn.

## Notes
### People who deserve assistance
The Prophet (S.A.W) taught that asking people for money is not allowed except in three situations (Sahih Muslim):

- A debtor: a person who is carrying a heavy debt that he cannot pay. He may seek help until the debt is settled, then he should stop.
- A person struck by disaster: someone whose property has been destroyed by a flood, fire, drought or another calamity. He may seek help until he can stand on his own again.
- A destitute person: someone who is truly poor and does not have enough for basic needs. Responsible people in the community should be able to confirm that the need is real. He may seek help until he has enough, then he should stop.

These are the people Muslims should support with zakat, sadaqah and other help. Helping them is an act of kindness and worship.

### Why people beg
Some people beg because of real poverty, debt, sickness, old age, being an orphan, or losing property in a disaster. Others beg out of laziness, or because begging has become a habit, even though they could work. A Muslim should know the difference. The design of this lesson calls us to self-awareness: we avoid begging when we have no real justification.

### Evils of begging
- It lowers a person's dignity. The Prophet (S.A.W) said that the upper hand is better than the lower hand (Bukhari and Muslim). The upper hand is the one that gives; the lower hand is the one that asks.
- It can make a person stop trying. A habit of begging weakens hard work.
- It may involve lying, if someone pretends to be poorer than he is.
- It can take help away from people who are truly desperate.
- Begging without a real need is unlawful. The Prophet (S.A.W) taught that, apart from the three cases above, the person who begs is taking what is not allowed.

Islam wants every Muslim who is able to work to earn, and wants the community to carry those who truly cannot.

## Key words
• debtor — a person who owes money that he or she must pay back
• destitute — a person who is extremely poor and lacks basic needs
• disaster — a sudden event such as a flood or fire that destroys property
• begging — asking people for money or food instead of earning it

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A trader's shop burns down and he has no goods left. His neighbour is healthy but refuses to look for work and asks people for money every day. Who deserves assistance, and why?

Working:
1. The trader lost his property through a disaster. He is in one of the three groups the Prophet (S.A.W) named.
2. The healthy neighbour can work. Begging without a real need is discouraged.

Answer: The trader deserves help until he can trade again. The neighbour should work instead of begging.

## Activity: Who should we support?
You will need: Exercise book, Manila paper
1. In groups, list the three categories of people who deserve support: debtors, those who lose property through disaster, and the destitute.
2. For each category, give one example a learner might see in the community.
3. Discuss the evils of begging according to the teachings of Islam.
4. Write the points in your notebook and present them to the class, taking turns to speak.

## Practice
1. Name the three categories of people who may seek help according to the teaching of the Prophet (S.A.W).
2. What is meant by 'the upper hand is better than the lower hand'?
3. Give two evils of begging.
4. Why might a person beg after a flood destroys the family farm?

## Summary
• Debtors, victims of disaster and the destitute deserve help.
• Begging is not allowed for a person who can earn.
• The giving hand is better than the asking hand.

### Answers to practice
1. A person with a heavy debt, a person whose property is destroyed by a disaster, and a person who is truly destitute.
2. The hand that gives is better than the hand that asks.
3. Any two: it lowers dignity; it discourages hard work; it may involve lying; it can take help from the truly needy; begging without need is unlawful.
4. The family has lost its property through a disaster and may need help until they can stand again.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Honest work as a way out of poverty

LESSON 2: HONEST WORK AS A WAY OUT OF POVERTY
=============================================

## What you will learn
• Describe ways of earning an honest income.
• Explain how work helps to eradicate poverty.
• Show appreciation for hard work in daily life.

Curriculum outcomes: b) describe the evils of begging as a means of fostering hard work; c) appreciate work as a means of eradicating poverty

## Introduction
The Prophet (S.A.W) honoured people who earned their food with their own hands. A small honest job is better than stretching out a hand when you are able to work.

## Notes
### Work is honourable
The Prophet (S.A.W) said that nobody has ever eaten better food than what he earned by the work of his own hands, and that Prophet Dawud (A.S.) used to eat from the work of his hands (Bukhari). He also taught that it is better for a person to take a rope, collect firewood, carry it and sell it than to beg from people who may give or refuse (Bukhari).

These teachings foster hard work. A Muslim does not look down on a lawful job, even if it looks simple.

### Ways of earning income
People generate income in many lawful ways:

- Farming: growing crops such as maize, beans, vegetables or fruit and selling the surplus.
- Keeping livestock: cows, goats, sheep or poultry for milk, meat or eggs.
- Trade: buying goods and selling them in a shop or at the market.
- Crafts: tailoring, carpentry, pottery, weaving or repairing items.
- Employment: working for a person, a farm, a school or a company and receiving wages.
- Services: teaching, cutting hair, washing clothes, or transporting goods.

A child in Grade 4 is not expected to run a business. You prepare for work by studying, helping with chores, learning a skill from a parent or relative, and refusing to ask for money you do not need.

### How work eradicates poverty
- Work puts food on the table without depending on begging.
- A working person can save a little and meet needs such as school, medicine and shelter.
- Workers can give sadaqah and become the upper hand.
- Honest work builds the family and the nation, because goods and services are produced.
- It protects dignity and teaches responsibility and integrity.

Poverty is not removed by wishing. It is reduced when people who can work do so, and when the community supports those who truly cannot. A Muslim thanks Allah for strength and uses that strength to earn.

## Key words
• income — money earned from work, trade or another lawful source
• poverty — the state of not having enough for basic needs
• sadaqah — voluntary charity given to please Allah
• lawful (halal) — allowed in Islam

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Yusuf wants new shoes. He can ask strangers for coins, or he can help his uncle in the vegetable stall on Saturday and save what he is given. Which choice agrees with Islamic teaching?

Working:
1. He is not a debtor, a disaster victim or destitute. He wants something extra.
2. Helping at the stall is honest work and keeps his dignity.

Answer: He should help his uncle and save, instead of begging.

## Activity: Ways of earning
You will need: Exercise book, Pictures of farms, markets and crafts if available
1. In pairs, list as many lawful ways of earning or generating income as you can.
2. Choose three and say what skill or tool each one needs.
3. Discuss how each kind of work can help a family leave poverty.
4. Present your list in class and write it in your notebook.

## Practice
1. What did the Prophet (S.A.W) say is better than begging: selling firewood, or sitting and asking people?
2. Name three lawful ways of earning income.
3. Give two ways in which work helps to eradicate poverty.
4. What can a Grade 4 learner do now to value work?

## Summary
• The best food is what a person earns with his or her own hands.
• Farming, trade, crafts, employment and services are lawful ways to earn.
• Honest work reduces poverty and lets a Muslim help others.

### Answers to practice
1. Collecting firewood and selling it is better than begging.
2. Any three: farming, keeping livestock, trade, crafts such as tailoring or carpentry, employment for wages, or offering a service.
3. Any two: it provides food and needs without begging; a person can save; workers can help others; it produces goods and services; it protects dignity.
4. Study hard, help with chores, learn a skill, and avoid asking for money without a real need.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 5.2.1 PROHIBITIONS IN ISLAM: EVILS OF BEGGING
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which person deserves assistance according to the teaching studied?
   A. A healthy person who dislikes work
   B. A family whose house and goods were destroyed by a flood
   C. A learner who wants sweets
   D. A trader who wants a second shop for pride

2. A debtor may seek help until…
   A. he becomes the richest person in town
   B. the debt is settled
   C. people get tired of him
   D. he stops praying

3. Who is a destitute person?

4. The upper hand is better than the lower hand. Which hand is the upper hand?
   A. asks
   B. gives
   C. points
   D. hides

5. Which of these is an evil of begging?
   A. It builds dignity
   B. It can become a habit that stops a person from working
   C. It always pleases Allah
   D. It is the same as zakat

6. Why is pretending to be poor in order to get money wrong?

7. According to the Hadith, which food is the best?
   A. Food received by begging
   B. Food earned by one's own hands
   C. Food taken by force
   D. Food left on the road

8. Which of these is a lawful way of generating income?
   A. Stealing
   B. Tailoring and selling clothes
   C. Cheating buyers
   D. Begging while able to work

9. How does honest work help to eradicate poverty?

10. What should a person do after receiving enough help to stand again?
   A. Keep begging every day
   B. Stop asking and work if able
   C. Hide the help
   D. Refuse to thank Allah
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 5.2.1 PROHIBITIONS IN ISLAM: EVILS OF BEGGING
========================================

1. B. A family whose house and goods were destroyed by a flood
   Loss of property through disaster is one of the three situations in which help may be sought.

2. B. the debt is settled
   Help for a debtor is until the heavy debt is paid, then he should stop asking.

3. A person who is extremely poor and lacks basic needs.
   The destitute are among those who deserve support.

4. B. gives
   The Prophet (S.A.W) praised the hand that gives over the hand that receives.

5. B. It can become a habit that stops a person from working
   Begging without need weakens hard work and lowers dignity.

6. It is a lie, and it can take help away from people who are truly in need.
   Islam forbids lying and wants charity to reach those who deserve it.

7. B. Food earned by one's own hands
   The Prophet (S.A.W) said nobody has eaten better food than what he earned by his own work.

8. B. Tailoring and selling clothes
   Crafts such as tailoring are honest work.

9. It provides for needs, allows saving, and lets a person help others instead of depending on begging.
   Work is the means Islam encourages for removing poverty.

10. B. Stop asking and work if able
   The permission to ask ends when the need has been met.
